questions.question: B has 32 pens, 24 pencils and 16 erasers. How many sets of these three items can be made without any left over?
questions.solution:
We know,

To make 3 items of B without any left over, take HCF of 32,24 and 16

Factors of 32 = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32

Factors of 24 = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24

Factors of 16 = 1, 2, 4, 4,8, 16

⇒ HCF = 8

Number of sets of 1st item = 32/8 = 4

Number of sets of 2nd item = 24/8 = 3

Number of sets of 3rd item = 16/8 = 2

Total sets = 4 + 3 + 2 

**∴ Number of sets of three items that can be made by B without any left over are 9 sets.**

questions.question: The population of a village increases by 0.2% in the first year, it increases by 0.4% in the second year, and due to some disease, it decreases by 0.4% in the third year. questions.solution:
**Concept:**

To find the population after n years,

Multiply the initial population by (1 + annual growth rate)ⁿ.

**Solution:**

After the first year: 2000 × (1 + 0.002) = 2004.

After the second year: 2004 × (1 + 0.004) = 2012.02.

After the third year: 2012.02 × (1 - 0.004) = 2003.97.

**Therefore, the population of the village after 3 years will be approximately 2003.97.**

questions.question: A tap can fill a tank in 6 hours. After half the tank is filled, three more similar taps are opened. What is the total time taken for the tank to get filled?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by one tap to fill the tank = 6 hours.

After half the tank is filled, three more similar taps are opened.

**Formula Used:**

Total Time = Time taken to fill half the tank + Time taken to fill the remaining half with four taps.

**Calculation:**

Time taken to fill half the tank by one tap = 6 / 2 = 3 hours.

Rate of filling by one tap = 1/6 tank/hour.

Rate of filling by four taps = 4 × (1/6) = 4/6 = 2/3 tank/hour.

Time taken to fill the remaining half by four taps:

Remaining half of the tank = 1/2 tank.

Time = (1/2) / (2/3)

⇒ Time = (1/2) × (3/2)

⇒ Time = 3/4 hours.

Total Time = 3 hours + 3/4 hours

⇒ Total Time = 3 hours + 0.75 hours

⇒ Total Time = 3.75 hours

⇒ Total Time = 3 hours 45 minutes

**The total time taken for the tank to get filled is 3 hours 45 minutes.**

⇒ Prime factorisation of 36 = 2² × 3²

⇒ Prime factorisation of 30 = 2 × 3 × 5

⇒ LCM (24, 36, 30) = Highest powers of all prime factors = 2³ × 3² × 5

⇒ LCM = 8 × 9 × 5 = 360 seconds

⇒ We know that 1 minute = 60 seconds

⇒ Time in minutes = 360 ÷ 60 = 6 minutes

Relative Speed on a Circular Track

questions.question: A person has to cover a distance of 8 km in 1 hour. If he covers one-fourth of the distance in one-third of the total time, then what should his speed (in km/h) be to cover the remaining distance in the remaining time so that the person reaches the destination exactly on time?

Total Distance = 8 km

Speed = Distance / Time

Distance covered in one-third of the time:

⇒ Distance₁ = 1/4 × 8 km = 2 km

Time taken to cover 2 km:

⇒ Time₁ = 1/3 × 1 hour = 1/3 hour

Remaining distance to be covered:

⇒ Distance₂ = 8 km - 2 km = 6 km

⇒ Time₂ = 1 hour - 1/3 hour = 2/3 hour

Required speed to cover the remaining distance in the remaining time:

⇒ Speed = Distance₂ / Time₂

⇒ Speed = 6 km / (2/3) hour

⇒ Speed = 6 km × 3/2

⇒ Speed = 9 km/h

**∴ The required speed is 9 km/h.**

questions.question: The potential difference, V, across the ends of a given metallic wire in an electric circuit is directly proportional to the current flowing through it, provided its temperature remains the same. This is called ______ law.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Ohm's**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The relationship between current, voltage, and resistance is described by Ohm's law. This law is given by George Simon Ohm in 1828

Ohm’s law:__

__
 
• Ohm’s law states that at a constant temperature, the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• Voltage = Current × Resistance
 
 
• V = I × R
 
• V = voltage, I = current and R = resistance
 
 
 
• The SI unit of resistance is ohms and is denoted by Ω.
 
• It helps to calculate the power, efficiency, current, voltage, and resistance of an element of an electrical circuit.
 
• If an element follows ohm’s law, then the element is known as a linear element.
 
• Ex: Resistor

Limitation of ohm's Law:__

__
 
• Ohm’s law is applicable for conductors only.
 
• Ohm’s law does not apply to unilateral networks. Unilateral networks allow the current to flow in one direction. Such types of networks consist of elements like a diode, transistor, etc.
 
• Ohm’s law is also not applicable to non - linear elements.
 
• Non-linear elements are those which do not have current exactly proportional to the applied voltage that means the resistance value of those elements changes for different values of voltage and current. An example of a non-linear element is a thyristor.
 
• Ohm’s law is also not applicable to vacuum tubes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Boyle’s Law**

 
• ​Boyle's law is a gas law that states that a gas's pressure and volume are inversely proportional.
 
• It states that at a constant temperature, the pressure exerted by a gas is inversely proportional to the volume occupied by it.
 
• According to the Boyle's Law:
 
 
• P1V1 = P2V2
 
 
• Where P1 = Initial Pressure

 P2 = Final Pressure

 V1 = Initial Volume 

 V2 = Final Volume

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/883ca4a9c62fe7d942ab5573518c8cee4603dd50fc0953b220b928a0f514f177.png] 
 
 
 
 

The five main gas laws in chemistry are Boyle's Law, Charle's Law, Gay Lussac's Law, Avogadro's Law, and Ideal Gas Law.

 
• Charle's law states that the volume of an ideal gas is directly proportional to the absolute temperature at constant pressure.
 
• Gay-Lussac's law states that the pressure of a given mass of gas varies directly with the absolute temperature of the gas when the volume is kept constant.
 
• Avogadro's law or Avogadro-Ampère's hypothesis is an experimental gas law relating the volume of a gas to the amount of substance of gas present.
 
• The ideal gas law states that the product of the pressure and the volume of one gram molecule of an ideal gas is equal to the product of the absolute temperature of the gas and the universal gas constant.

The ratio of the area of a square to that of the square drawn on its diagonal.

Side of the new square which is drawn on the diagonal of the old square = The diagonal of the old square

Side of new square = √2a

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some pins are clips.

Some clips are bands.

Conclusions:

I. No pins are bands.

II. At least some pins are bands.

options.text: Either conclusion I or II follows
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c2e5dbac2a0563958004021ecd42ca9869d2954898ea2e27599f1f4787810cb.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No pins are bands → Does not follow (As some pins are clips, some clips are bands. So, no pins are bands is possible but not definitely true)

II. At least some pins are bands → Does not follow (As some pins are clips, some clips are bands. So, some pins are bands is possible but not definitely true)

∴ Here,

 
• Elements i.e pins and bands are same in both the conclusions.
 
• Both the conclusions are individually does not follow.
 
• Conclusion I and II are complementary pair i.e one of the conclusion is negative and one of the conclusion is positive. 

Hence, the correct answer is "Either conclusion I or II follows".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 Conditions of either or case

 
• The elements should be same in both the conclusions
 
• Both conclusions should possible but not definitely true.
 
• One of the conclusion should be negative and one of the conclusion should be positive i.e complimentary pair.
 
• Complimentary pairs :​

 
• ​some + no and all + some not
 
• Some + Some not and All + no are not Complimentary pair.
